analysis:
The supplied units are head-side text of docs/architecture/inference.md (lines 416-1208). The patch itself adds only documentation about Flint constrained-decode chaining and fused decode kernels (head lines ~2492-2512, outside the supplied excerpts but visible in the patch). No code, config, auth, crypto, or protocol behavior changes in this PR, so no control is weakened.

I checked the supplied prose against the threat model. Prefix-cache statements are consistent with T-041. Coordinator text prefix reuse is partitioned by the authenticated cache scope and is off without one (line ~528). The Nemotron slot emits no cache receipts or prefix-cache capability. Media requests are excluded from prefix lookup and capture (line ~829). The SSD stage description is unchanged in kind. Nothing here loosens the 30-minute TTL, the HMAC lookup tags, the salt scoping or the KEK-based purge.

The media and audio ingress paragraphs (rejection of unsupported input_audio before model acquisition, 400 for oversized or invalid media) describe fail-closed behavior and match the T-050 and TB-007 posture. The App Attest and TB-011 boundaries are not touched.

The new Flint text says the maskCacheKey is the constraint state and that repeated states reuse a cached device mask. The doc says the token stream is identical to unchained decode. Whether the mask cache is isolated per request or per cache scope cannot be verified from docs alone. The claim is a performance optimization on the mask, not on tenant data, and the key is the state alone, so cross-tenant leakage is unlikely.

The doc claims the Flint decode kernels produce byte-identical outputs. This is unverified and not a security regression. Code review of the underlying Swift changes, which are outside this batch, would need to confirm that retained logits and RNG restoration do not retain sensitive state longer than allowed (T-028). No findings.
